clue.text: Dreadfully offend a tar everywhere on board

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is botched and jumbled, so the following letters come out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written; a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Some passenger manages to upset a sailor wherever he goes on the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, fore is the front and aft the rear, so from front to back covers the whole vessel.

clue.text: Show great affection for young animal

blocks.note: first meaning: to fuss over someone, usually to curry favour
second meaning: a baby deer

explanation.surface: Someone dotes on a baby animal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to flatter or make a servile fuss over someone; as a noun it is a deer in its first year.

clue.text: Interpret article in Russian

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, so the article is placed inside the other word

blocks.note: Red was the label for a Soviet Russian, from the Communist red flag
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A translator works on an article written in Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a situation or text is to understand it a particular way, the same as interpreting it.

clue.text: Old hero's sole weakness? Yes and no

blocks.note: setter's reading: the one vulnerable spot of a Greek warrior, at the back of his foot
surface reading: an equivocal answer to the question; really it says the phrase is literally true of the hero and figurative for anyone else

explanation.walkthrough: Sole puns on the foot: the weak spot was not the sole but close to it, hence yes and no.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles' mother dipped him in the Styx holding his heel, so it was his one vulnerable spot; the phrase now means any fatal flaw.

clue.text: At meeting. American might tip this for the big race

blocks.note: first meaning: the American name for a bowler hat, which one tips in greeting
second meaning: the famous flat race run at Epsom

explanation.surface: At the racecourse, an American gives a betting tip for the main event.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip looks like a betting tip at a race meeting, but it is raising a hat in greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a bowler hat is called by this name, and in Britain it is the Epsom classic for three-year-olds.

clue.text: Going to fire from this vessel? That's even more dangerous

definitions.text: Going to fire from this vessel? That's even more dangerous

blocks.clueFragment: Going to fire from this vessel?
blocks.note: surface reading: a warship about to open fire
setter's reading: the proverb about leaving a bad situation for a worse one, the vessel being a cooking pot

explanation.walkthrough: Vessel and fire suggest a gunship, but the vessel is kitchenware and the fire is the proverb's.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of the pan and into the fire describes escaping one danger only to land in a greater one.

clue.text: Outside parts of cake I had covered thus?

definitions.text: Outside parts of cake I had covered thus?

indicators.note: the outside parts of a word are its first and last letters, leaving the middle behind
one piece covers another by wrapping around it, so the contraction for I had goes around the kept letters

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
the first and last letters of cake

explanation.surface: A baker describes the outside of a cake she has finished decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a cake whose outside has been covered in icing is iced.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake with a sugary coating spread over its exterior is described as iced, which is the covering the clue implies.

clue.text: Church left room for varying number

definitions.note: read as numb-er, something that makes you numb

indicators.note: things that vary change form, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church has left space for a variable congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: Number is not a figure here but something that numbs, a classic crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: This anaesthetic was once used to render patients unconscious and senseless, so it is a numbing agent.

clue.text: Flower mother, on request, got out of bed

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
to ask is to request
rose is the past tense of rise, to get up

explanation.surface: Mother asked someone to fetch a flower before she got up.
explanation.definitionFit: The damask is an old fragrant variety of garden rose, prized for its scented pink petals.

clue.text: Said whether I could provide meteorological expertise

definitions.note: used loosely: a weather eye is a skill at reading coming conditions

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we want words that sound like the following ones rather than spell them

blocks.note: whether sounds like the word for the climate, and I like the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they could offer their expertise as a weather forecaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a weather eye means watching the sky for changes, a forecasting skill sailors relied on.

clue.text: Poor-quality houses endlessly collapse

definitions.note: plural against a singular answer: a slum is an area of such houses

indicators.note: without an end, the final letter of the following word is cut off

blocks.note: a slump is a collapse, as in prices

explanation.surface: Shoddily built houses keep falling down.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum is a squalid, overcrowded district of run-down housing in a town or city.

clue.text: One must be behind the lines before action can start

definitions.text: One must be behind the lines before action can start

blocks.clueFragment: One must be behind the lines before action can start
blocks.note: surface reading: a soldier who must be behind enemy lines before an operation begins

blocks.clueFragment: One must be behind the lines before action can start
blocks.note: setter's reading: the person responsible for an actor's lines, needed before a director calls action

explanation.walkthrough: Lines and action sound military, but they are dialogue and the director's call on a film set.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialogue must be written before filming begins, so its author is behind the lines spoken on set.

clue.text: Portraying eccentrics, some of Carroll's characters

blocks.note: an actor portraying a part is playing it
a card is an eccentric or comic person

explanation.surface: An actor takes on oddball roles from Lewis Carroll's books.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland, the Queen of Hearts and her court, gardeners and soldiers are a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's Wonderland is peopled partly by a living pack, the Queen of Hearts and her suited soldiers and gardeners.

clue.text: Apt to be shot?

blocks.note: surface reading: likely to be killed by gunfire
setter's reading: well suited to being photographed

explanation.walkthrough: Shot suggests a gun, but a shot is also a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks good in pictures suits the camera, so is well fitted to being snapped.

clue.text: Tradesman rearranging morning round with hesitation

indicators.note: rearranging means putting things in a new order, so the letters that follow are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
O is round in shape
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper hesitantly reorganises his morning delivery round.
explanation.walkthrough: An ironmonger is the British name for a hardware dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a shopkeeper, and this one sells tools, nails and other hardware.

clue.text: Beat up?

blocks.note: surface reading: give someone a thrashing
setter's reading: a tool for beating a mount to urge it on, as with gee up

explanation.walkthrough: Beat up reads as an assault, but up is also what a rider calls to get a horse moving.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a long whip used on a horse, and as a verb means to flog someone with one.

clue.text: As director, prepare to shoot after hold-up

blocks.note: a hitch is a delay or hold-up
to cock a gun is to ready it for firing

explanation.surface: A film director gets ready to start shooting after a delay on set.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the gun piece second. Shoot looks like filming, but it is firing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock was the English film-maker behind Psycho and The Birds.

clue.text: Gather fine ordered by king

indicators.note: letters that are ordered have been arranged afresh, so they are rearranged here

blocks.note: taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king has imposed a fine on someone, and the news gets round.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather in the sense of conclude or deduce from evidence, as in I gather you're leaving.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation hard to find after nine

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the ordinal that follows ninth

blocks.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Campers find it hard to get a pitch after nine at night.
explanation.definitionFit: In any sequence the position that directly follows the ninth is the tenth, so it comes after nine.

clue.text: Instruct drunk about English drinks

definitions.note: a tincture is also a small drink of spirits

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the word before is jumbled
about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A tipsy instructor is lecturing on English drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tincture is an old jocular word for a nip of alcohol, so tinctures are small alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Where all the world was a stage?

definitions.text: Where all the world was a stage?

blocks.clueFragment: Where all the world was a stage?
blocks.note: surface reading: Shakespeare's line from As You Like It, all the world's a stage

blocks.clueFragment: Where all the world was a stage?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a playhouse named after the world, so the world itself was where actors performed

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags wordplay on the quotation: the playhouse was named after the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's company performed at the London playhouse whose name means the world, so there the world literally was a stage.

clue.text: She's here today, gone tomorrow

blocks.note: surface reading: a fickle woman who never stays
setter's reading: a month with a girl's name, which ended on the day after this puzzle appeared

explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle was printed on 30 April 1998, so the month was here that day and gone the next.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a woman's name and the month whose last day was the date of publication.

clue.text: Scandinavian destroyer left Fair Isle

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
fair, meaning acceptable, is OK
I is the abbreviation for isle or island

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian warship has departed from Fair Isle, a remote Shetland island.
explanation.walkthrough: Destroyer looks like a warship, but it is a trickster god who brings about the gods' doom.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the mischief-making god causes Baldur's death and fights the gods at Ragnarok, the world's end.

clue.text: Composer looked up to in Africa

blocks.note: first meaning: Alban ..., the Austrian composer of Wozzeck
second meaning: a mountain in South Africa, from the Afrikaans word

explanation.surface: A composer is held in high regard in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Looked up to sounds like admired, but a mountain is literally looked up at; berg is the Afrikaans word, as in Drakensberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg wrote the opera Wozzeck, and in South African usage a mountain is called by this name.

clue.text: Almost dark, but not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of the word is used, so its final letter is lost

blocks.note: night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: It is almost dark outside, though not completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old adverb for nearly, as in well nigh impossible.

clue.text: Engine crewmen gently brush

blocks.note: a four is a rowing boat with four crewmen
to stroke is to brush lightly with the hand

explanation.surface: The engine-room crew softly brush something down.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroke is also the rower who sets the pace, which keeps the surface in the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-stroke is an internal combustion engine whose cycle takes four piston movements.

clue.text: One gets stuck in bottleneck here in Ireland

blocks.note: first meaning: the stopper pushed into the neck of a bottle
second meaning: a city and county in the south of Ireland

explanation.surface: A driver complains about being caught in a traffic jam in an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottleneck suggests traffic congestion, but it is taken literally as the neck of a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The stopper is made from oak bark of that name, and the Irish place is the Republic's second city.

clue.text: Indulging in horseplay with the blue poet? Good!

blocks.note: the blue is the sky
Philip Larkin, the English poet
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone praises a mournful poet for fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: The blue poet hints at a melancholy writer, apt for Larkin, but the blue is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylarking is boisterous fooling around, originally sailors' frolicking in the rigging.
